newsitem.title: USA: Medicare trust fund may go bankrupt by 2001 - trustees.
newsitem.headline: Medicare trust fund may go bankrupt by 2001 - trustees.

text.p: Medicare trustees Thursday predicted that without corrective legislation the program's hospital insurance trust fund would be depleted in 2001, a projected date of bankruptcy unchanged from last year's trustee's report.
"Today's report makes clear that the time to act to preserve Medicare is now," Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala said in a statement.
The trustees called for a national advisory group on Medicare reform to examine the program and make recommendations for long-term change.
President Bill Clinton's balanced budget plan calls for a $100 billion, five-year reduction in Medicare.
Congressional Republicans in the past have called for more aggressive action to preserve Medicare.

Medicare hospital insurance helps pay for care given by hospitals, skilled nursing facilities and other health facilities. Medicare trustees include Shalala, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and other administration officials and public members.
